title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.63). K is a field of finite type over Q, S is a normal model of K (scheme of finite type over Z with function field K), and U_K is an elementary anabelian (hyperbolic) curve that extends to a relative curve U_S over S. Here U_S is the complement in a proper smooth curve \hat U_S/S of a divisor S' = \hat U_S \ U_S that is finite étale over S.

This gives the extension (4): 1 → π → E_{U_S} = π_1(U_S) → E_S = π_1(S) → 1, with π the geometric fundamental group of a fibre. The extension E_{U_K} → E_K is obtained from (4) by fibre product along the surjection E_K = G_K → E_S.

Hence sections of E_{U_K} → E_K are the continuous lifts G_K → E_{U_S} of G_K → π_1(S). The lifts that are trivial on ker(G_K → π_1(S)), i.e. 'unramified over S', are exactly the sections of (4).

This page draws the consequence of the section conjecture, including cuspidal sections, for sections of (4). There are exactly two kinds.

1°) Sections coming from K-points of U_K, i.e. rational sections S ⇢ U_S. Grothendieck first wrote that every rational section works, crossed out 'rationnelle', and replaced it with 'régulière'. The corrected claim is that a K-point gives a section of (4) only if it is a regular (everywhere defined) section S → U_S.
- Mechanism: if the closure of the point meets the cusp divisor S' over a height-one prime p, then the restriction of the Galois section to the inertia at p maps nontrivially into a cuspidal inertia group, so the section is ramified.
- Conversely, a regular section S → U_S induces π_1(S) → π_1(U_S) by functoriality.
- So this is an 'integral' or 'S-integral points' form of the section conjecture: unramified non-cuspidal sections ↔ U_S(S).

2°) Cuspidal sections. These come from cusps i ∈ I(U_{\bar K}) rational over K, i.e. from sections S → S' of the finite étale cusp scheme. Grothendieck leaves open two questions:
- under what condition such a cusp gives a nonempty packet of splittings of (4);
- how to determine the packet exactly.

A natural answer, consistent with his framework but not written on this page:
- The cusp section σ: S → \hat U_S has a normal line bundle N on S.
- The 'punctured tubular neighbourhood' gives a decomposition-group extension 1 → \hat Z(1) → D_σ → π_1(S) → 1, whose class is (up to sign) the Chern class c_1(N) in H^2(S, \hat Z(1)).
- The packet is nonempty iff this class vanishes.
- When nonempty, the packet is a torsor under H^1(S, \hat Z(1)), which is an extension of T\hat Pic(S) by the completion of O(S)^*. Over K this becomes the familiar Kummer torsor under the completion of K^*.

The page closes by postponing these 'technical' points. Grothendieck turns instead to reconstructing the category of anabelian varieties over Q from Galois data (next page).
errors: The first draft ('section rationnelle') was wrong, and Grothendieck himself corrected it to 'régulière'. Strictly, what matters is codimension one: by Zariski–Nagata purity for regular S, a K-point whose closure avoids the cusps at all height-one primes gives a section unramified over S. Extending the point to an actual S-morphism then needs extra hypotheses (S regular, or the extension property of rational maps into relative curves of genus ≥1 / with no rational curves in fibres). For a merely normal S, 'régulière' should be read as 'regular in codimension 1', or S should be assumed regular.
The cuspidal case is explicitly unresolved on the page. The nonemptiness of the packet is a genuine obstruction (a Chern class in H^2(S, \hat Z(1))), not automatic as it is over a field.

ideas.what: Sections of π_1(U_S) → π_1(S) for a relative hyperbolic curve over an arithmetic model S correspond to unramified Galois sections over K. Conjecturally, the non-cuspidal ones correspond to S-integral points U_S(S).
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture for integral (S-integral) points; unramified sections; good-reduction / integrality criterion for sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in later work on the section conjecture (e.g. Stix's monograph on rational points and fundamental groups; Kim's nonabelian Chabauty uses π_1 of integral models)
ideas.where_published: The letter to Faltings (1983) states the section conjecture over finitely generated fields; I am unsure it contains this integral-model formulation.

ideas.what: Cuspidal sections attached to K-rational cusps, i.e. sections of the étale cusp scheme S' over S, and the question of when they give splittings of the integral extension (4).
ideas.modern_name: Cuspidal sections / packets of cuspidal sections over an integral base
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cuspidal sections: Grothendieck (letter to Faltings), later Nakamura, Stix, Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings mentions sections at infinity (unsure of the details)

ideas.what: Base-change description of E_{U_K} as the fibre product of E_{U_S} with G_K over π_1(S); lifts trivial on the kernel ↔ sections over π_1(S).
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental exact sequence of a relative curve and its base change to the generic point

missed.claim: Grothendieck asks when a K-rational cusp (a section of S' over S) gives a nonempty packet of splittings of π_1(U_S) → π_1(S), and how to describe that packet. The natural answer is: nonempty iff the Chern class of the normal bundle of the cusp section vanishes in H^2(S, \hat Z(1)); the packet is then a torsor under H^1(S, \hat Z(1)), i.e. the completion of O(S)^* extended by T\hat Pic(S). The thread is left open on the page.
missed.quote: Et il faudrait étudier encore à quelle condition une telle section définit un paquet non vide de scindages de (4) — et comment déterminer exactement tous ces scindages.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links the integral section conjecture to Picard groups and units of arithmetic schemes. For S = Spec Z[1/N] and U = P^1 \ {0,1,∞}, the non-cuspidal side is the S-unit equation. This is at most a modest addition, since cuspidal sections over integral bases have been treated in later work.

missed.claim: Under the conjectures, unramified Galois sections of an integral model ↔ S-integral points plus cuspidal packets. This ties anabelian geometry to Diophantine finiteness of integral points (Siegel, S-unit equations), anticipating the integral-points viewpoint of nonabelian Chabauty.
missed.quote: qu'une telle section rationnelle ne correspond effectivement à une section de l'extension (4), que si c'est une section régulière
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck formulated an integral-model version of the section conjecture in 1981. The formulation itself is now known in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sets out an early, explicit integral-model (S-integral points) form of the section conjecture, with a dichotomy between regular sections and cuspidal packets. It also poses an open question about cusp packets over S. This is a nice historical detail, but the mathematics is now fairly standard among specialists and the open point has a natural Kummer/Chern-class answer.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'de $E_{U_S}$ sur $U_S$' should read 'de $E_{U_S}$ sur $E_S$' (sections of the extension (4) over π_1(S)); the handwriting is ambiguous, but the mathematics requires E_S.
'sans mal, sans doute' is correct; the crossed-out word is 'rationnelle', replaced by underlined 'régulière'.
'{+l'extension+} (4)' is an insertion above the line, correctly rendered.
